targetAudience: Scientifically curious readers, students, science communicators and community participants seeking educational interpretation of a published paper, not personal medical or human-performance advice.
bestFor: One agreed research-literacy question anchored to one published paper, discussed in the existing 60-minute individual session with a proposed durable written question map.
prework: State the educational question and intended use without asking what you personally should take or do.
Provide the anchor paper link, DOI or PMID where available, and the claim or passage that needs interpretation.
Explain what you think the paper establishes and what remains uncertain.
Confirm source accessibility and disclose missing or inaccessible material without sending personal medical or sensitive information.
Confirm acceptance of the educational scope and the exclusion of diagnosis, prescribing, compound administration, dosing and personalised human-performance protocols.
outcomes: A written question map recording the agreed question, source identity, exact entity, model or population, comparator and measured endpoint.
A source-linked evidence read separating reported findings, limitations, unsupported interpretations and missing information.
A next-reading shortlist and clear close, self-directed reading route or optional separately quoted project scope.
scopeLimits: One agreed educational question and anchor paper; a fresh literature landscape or additional research question requires separate scope.
No exhaustive search, systematic review, formal meta-analysis or guarantee of a definitive conclusion.
No diagnosis, prescribing, compound administration or dosing, personal treatment decisions or personalised cognition, recovery, longevity or other human-performance protocols.
No supplier or batch verification, product efficacy endorsement, research-material eligibility change, credential or private-community entitlement.
Written-output timing and factual-correction terms must be agreed; ongoing advice and new analysis are not included by default.
The catalogue checkout flag does not establish operational payment or scheduling; a site purchase does not reserve a calendar slot.
process: Review the supplied question and source for educational fit before any booking or payment commitment.
Agree the narrow scope, written-output format, terms and scheduling through an operational owner-approved route.
Use the existing 60-minute session to examine entity, model, endpoint, findings, limitations and open questions.
Provide the agreed written question map and next-reading route, making inaccessible or unresolved evidence explicit.
Handle factual corrections within agreed terms; discuss wider work only through an optional separate quote.
bookingCta: Discuss one research question and confirm scope and availability. The existing price is €200; payment credentials are unavailable in the recovered environment, and payment and scheduling must be confirmed separately.

targetAudience: Science communicators, educators and research-oriented organisations needing a bounded, citation-linked educational briefing for a defined reader or internal research question.
bestFor: An agreed evidence question that needs a documented source set and synthesis beyond an individual paper walkthrough.
prework: Define the single evidence question, intended audience and educational or internal research use.
Supply known references and identify the source, topic and date boundaries to be agreed.
Describe existing uncertainty and exclusions rather than seeking a predetermined conclusion.
Identify the person approving scope, quote and review, and confirm permission to use any non-public materials.
Agree the search or review approach, source budget, meetings, revision boundaries and delivery format before commitment.
outcomes: A dated source map documenting included references, search or review boundaries and unavailable material.
An evidence table preserving study type, entity relationship, reported finding and limitation together.
A written synthesis distinguishing supported statements, uncertainty and unanswered questions without implying exhaustive coverage.
The existing decision session focused on educational interpretation or an internal research workflow, with a written next-reading or research-question map.
scopeLimits: The starting price is indicative; the agreed question, source burden, meetings and revisions determine the final quote.
Additional questions, broader landscapes, changing source sets and additional review rounds require a scope change.
No formal systematic review, meta-analysis, clinical decision recommendation, trial-design sign-off or legal or regulatory opinion unless an entirely separate appropriate service is established.
No diagnosis, prescribing, compound administration or dosing, personal human-performance protocols or guaranteed conclusion.
Literature citations do not authenticate suppliers, verify batches, establish product safety or efficacy, or change research-material eligibility.
Timing and acceptance criteria must be agreed rather than inferred from catalogue duration labels.
process: Qualify the educational question, intended use, source permissions and reviewer feasibility.
Agree a statement of work, search or review boundaries, written outputs, acceptance criteria, timing and final quote.
Map the agreed sources and record entity, model, endpoint, finding, limitation and missing evidence.
Produce a traceable original synthesis and review it against the agreed source and method requirements.
Deliver the briefing and educational decision session; treat additional research as separately quoted work.
bookingCta: Discuss briefing scope. The existing starting price remains From €850; agree the question, timing and final quote before paying.

targetAudience: Bioscience, research-content and knowledge-work teams with an owned document-heavy task, permitted example data and people available for human review.
bestFor: Evaluating one bounded research-document workflow with a documented baseline, citation checks, explicit failure criteria and an agreed human-reviewed handoff.
prework: Name the workflow owner, intended users and the single task to be evaluated.
Describe the current process and supply baseline examples or measurements where available.
Provide authorised, non-sensitive sample inputs and confirm data permissions and confidentiality requirements.
Identify human reviewers, acceptable outputs and failure or escalation criteria.
Agree the proof-of-concept artifact, evaluation approach, tool constraints, exclusions and any separately authorised implementation work.
outcomes: A written baseline and task specification recording the workflow, source boundaries and review responsibilities.
A bounded proof-of-concept specification or agreed prototype artifact, subject to explicit authorisation and actual delivery capability.
An evaluation set, rubric and results record including failures, unsupported claims and citation-verification checks.
A reusable SOP and governance handoff covering access boundaries, human review, escalation and further implementation needs.
scopeLimits: One agreed document-heavy task; additional workflows, integrations or datasets require separate scope and permission.
No guarantee of accuracy, time savings, cost reduction, clinical effectiveness or production readiness.
No clinical decision system, diagnosis, prescribing, compound administration or dosing, or personalised human-performance advice.
No default ingestion of patient records, private Discord posts or unauthorised confidential material.
Production deployment, hosting, API connections, continuous monitoring, unlimited model tuning and ongoing support are not included by default.
Tool costs, reviewer availability, acceptance criteria and timing must be agreed in the final quote.
process: Qualify workflow ownership, data permissions, reviewer capability and fit for a bounded educational or research workflow.
Agree the task, baseline, evaluation criteria, deliverables, timing, permissions and final quote.
Document the baseline and prepare the agreed proof-of-concept specification or explicitly authorised artifact.
Evaluate against the agreed rubric with human review, source checks and an explicit failure record.
Deliver the SOP and governance handoff; quote broader implementation or continued support separately if appropriate.
bookingCta: Discuss one workflow and its evaluation scope. The existing starting price remains From €2,800; agree permissions, timing and the final quote before paying.

targetAudience: Bioscience, research-content and educational teams seeking a shared approach to search, source evaluation, prompting, retrieval-augmented generation and safe human-reviewed adoption.
bestFor: The existing half-day team working session around one approved case, with reusable materials for evidence checking and non-clinical AI workflow practice.
prework: Name the team sponsor and describe the shared learning objective and intended use.
Identify participant needs, familiarity with the tools and delivery format to be agreed.
Supply one approved team case and authorised, non-sensitive example documents.
Identify current search or source-checking difficulties and the methods the team wants to practise.
Agree participant scope, facilitator feasibility, customisation, tool access, exclusions and any travel or external costs before quoting.
outcomes: A case workbook recording the team's agreed research-literacy or document-workflow exercise.
A reusable SOP for source evaluation, prompting, citation verification and human review.
A quality rubric distinguishing traceable outputs from unsupported claims and model failures.
A written team adoption and next-action checklist, with optional separately quoted workflow evaluation where appropriate.
scopeLimits: An agreed half-day team workshop and approved case; participant scope and facilitator coverage require confirmation.
Additional cohorts, extensive bespoke research, travel, software costs and implementation work require explicit scope.
Attendance is not a credential or certification and does not guarantee competence, accuracy, productivity or effectiveness.
No diagnosis, prescribing, compound administration or dosing, clinical decision support or personalised human-performance protocols.
No patient records, private-community harvesting or unauthorised data use.
No default system deployment, continuous support or entitlement to external community access.
process: Qualify the sponsor, educational objective, participant needs, case permissions and facilitator feasibility.
Agree the team scope, learning exercise, materials, timing, exclusions and final quote.
Prepare the approved case and reusable source-evaluation and quality-checking materials.
Run the half-day working session with source checks, failure analysis and human-review practice.
Deliver the agreed workbook, SOP, rubric and action checklist; discuss a sprint only if a concrete owned workflow warrants one.
bookingCta: Discuss the team case and workshop scope. The existing starting price remains From €1,200; agree participants, timing and the final quote before paying.
